questions: Did the asymmetry begin suddenly, within the last 48 hours?
Do you have weakness or numbness in an arm or leg on the same side?
Do you have difficulty speaking or understanding speech?
Is the affected side of your face unable to wrinkle the forehead or fully close the eye?
Have you had ear pain, a rash near the ear, or a recent viral illness?
Have you had episodes of involuntary twitching or spasms on one side of the face?
Have you ever had a complete episode of facial weakness or facial paralysis on this side?
Do the facial spasms primarily involve forceful closure of one eye?
When you smile or blink, does the corner of your mouth on the same side move involuntarily?
Do the spasms occur in brief, irregular bursts rather than continuously?
Do the spasms worsen with stress, fatigue, or voluntary facial movements?
Have these spasms been present for more than three months?
Does the affected side of the face remain visibly weak or droopy between spasms?
Does the involuntary eye closure occur when you voluntarily smile, purse your lips, or wrinkle your nose?
Do the spasms involve only the eyelid, without twitching of the forehead or cheek?
Are the eye-closing movements rhythmic and repetitive, occurring many times per minute?
Do the spasms stop completely when you are asleep?
orders: Focused cranial-nerve examination documenting forehead movement, eye closure strength, smile symmetry, and synkinetic movements during forceful eye closure and smiling
Electromyography and facial-nerve conduction study, including blink-reflex testing, of both sides of the face
MRI of the brain and internal auditory canals with and without gadolinium contrast, focusing on the facial-nerve course and cerebellopontine angle
served: MRI brain and internal auditory canal with contrast
